I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My family has about 8 mu. My husband does some off-farm work in town now, so I manage most of the fieldwork myself, sometimes hiring day labor at harvest. At 55, I'm not going to change what works — around here, everyone grows wheat in winter and corn in summer on the same land. That's the rotation. The soil knows it, the market knows it, I know it.

For wheat I'll use the improved variety seeds I buy from the co-op in town — same ones I've used the last three years, good against rust. For corn I always buy hybrid seed bags, the郑单 type, from the same shop. I don't save seed.

Fertilizer: I apply compound fertilizer as base before sowing, then urea top-dressing at jointing for wheat, and chase-fertilize corn around the 10-leaf stage. I probably put on a bit more than I need to — my father taught me that skimping on fertilizer is skimping on the harvest.

For irrigation I pump from the village well. Wheat needs water before freeze, again at jointing, and at heading — three times minimum, four if spring is dry. Corn I mostly leave to rain except once if July is bad.

Pesticides: I spray herbicide on the wheat in spring, and a fungicide pass if I see any yellow rust or powdery mildew. For corn I do one herbicide pass right after emergence and watch for 玉米螟 — usually one insecticide spray.

Tillage: I do rotary tillage with the village's shared machine before each sowing. I haven't tried no-till — I don't trust it yet.
